pathophysiology.summary: Prelabour rupture of membranes (PROM) is rupture of the fetal membranes before the onset of labour; P-PROM is PROM before 37 weeks. Membrane weakening from infection/inflammation, stretch and collagen degradation leads to rupture; the main risks are ascending infection, cord prolapse, abruption and preterm birth.
keyMechanisms: Loss of the amniotic barrier allows ascending infection (chorioamnionitis) — the main maternal consequence (MOH).
Antibiotics after P-PROM prolong the latency period and improve neonatal outcomes.
Corticosteroids (24–34 weeks) reduce respiratory distress, intraventricular haemorrhage and necrotising enterocolitis.
Prolonged oligohydramnios at very early gestation risks pulmonary hypoplasia and limb contractures.
Term PROM: induction reduces time to birth and chorioamnionitis/endometritis (MOH).

symptoms: Sudden gush or continued leakage of fluid from the vagina.
Fever, offensive discharge or abdominal pain suggest infection.
physicalSigns: Pooling of amniotic fluid on sterile speculum; leakage on coughing.
Maternal fever, tachycardia, uterine tenderness, fetal tachycardia (chorioamnionitis).
redFlags: Signs of intra-amniotic infection → deliver regardless of gestation
Cord prolapse, significant abruption/bleeding, fetal compromise
precipitants: Genital tract infection; previous P-PROM or preterm birth.
Polyhydramnios, multiple pregnancy, cervical procedures, smoking.

differentials.condition: Urinary incontinence or increased vaginal discharge

ruleIn.modalityTarget: All with suspected rupture (avoid digital examination)
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Pooling seen → manage as P-PROM; no further test needed (NICE).

clinicalManagement.title: Confirm and look for reasons to deliver
actions: Speculum for pooling; IGFBP-1/PAMG-1 if none seen.
Deliver regardless of gestation if intra-amniotic infection, significant abruption, cord prolapse, active labour with severe bleeding, life-threatening maternal disease or fetal death (MOH).

clinicalManagement.title: P-PROM 24–33+6 weeks: expectant management
actions: Antibiotics: erythromycin 250 mg orally 4 times a day for up to 10 days or until established labour (NICE); oral penicillin if erythromycin not tolerated.

MOH alternative: ampicillin 2 g IV every 6 h + erythromycin 250 mg every 6 h for 48 h, then amoxicillin 250 mg + erythromycin 250 mg every 8 h for 5 days; penicillin allergy: clindamycin 900 mg IV every 8 h + gentamicin 7 mg/kg (ideal body weight) 2 doses 24 h apart, then clindamycin 300 mg orally every 8 h for 5 days.
Corticosteroids: dexamethasone 12 mg IM every 12 h × 2.
Magnesium neuroprotection if birth expected under 30 weeks (32 weeks per MOH).
Monitor for infection, abruption, cord prolapse and fetal wellbeing; consider delivery at 34 weeks (MOH).

clinicalManagement.title: P-PROM below 24 weeks
actions: Expectant management if stable; antibiotics and steroids not recommended before viability (MOH); outpatient follow-up possible, admit at viability.

clinicalManagement.title: Term PROM
actions: Induction of labour reduces time to birth and infection (MOH); no routine prophylactic antibiotics at term.

regimens.duration: Up to 10 days or until established labour
adjustments: Oral penicillin if erythromycin not tolerated
contraindications: With terfenadine, astemizole, cisapride, pimozide, ergotamine or dihydroergotamine
regimens.sourceTitle: NICE NG25: Preterm labour and birth

regimens.dose: Ampicillin 2 g IV every 6 h for 48 h; then amoxicillin 250 mg PO every 8 h for 5 days
adjustments: With erythromycin 250 mg (6-hourly IV phase, 8-hourly oral phase)
contraindications: Serious hypersensitivity to amoxicillin or other beta-lactams
regimens.sourceTitle: MOH Pocket Manual in Obstetrics & Gynaecology, Saudi Ministry of Health
regimens.useWhen: MOH regimen chosen instead of erythromycin

regimens.dose: Clindamycin 900 mg IV every 8 h for 48 h, then 300 mg PO every 8 h for 5 days; gentamicin 7 mg/kg (ideal body weight) 2 doses 24 h apart
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to gentamicin or other aminoglycosides
regimens.sourceTitle: MOH Pocket Manual in Obstetrics & Gynaecology, Saudi Ministry of Health

regimens.indication: Fetal lung maturation (24+0 to 33+6 weeks; consider to 35+6)
regimens.patientGroup: Pregnant women with threatened/planned preterm birth or P-PROM
regimens.duration: 2 doses (one course; at most one repeat course if more than 7 days and still under 34 weeks)
adjustments: MOH regimen; betamethasone is an alternative per local protocol
regimens.sourceTitle: MOH Pocket Manual in Obstetrics & Gynaecology, Saudi Ministry of Health

regimens.indication: Fetal neuroprotection (24+0 to 29+6 weeks; consider 30+0 to 33+6)
regimens.patientGroup: Established preterm labour or planned birth within 24 h
regimens.dose: 4 g IV bolus over 15 min, then 1 g/h
adjustments: Do not use beyond 24 h (MHRA: skeletal effects with prolonged use)
monitoring: Pulse, BP, RR, patellar reflexes at least every 4 h; urine output
regimens.sourceTitle: NICE NG25: Preterm labour and birth
